claude.sample_unit: patients (3,364 original and 35,457 augmented CT images)

links.outcome: Accuracy and AUC under leakage-free patient-wise split versus leaky image-level split
links.effect: Patient-wise: AUC 0.946, accuracy 0.905; leaky image-level split: accuracy 0.991, AUC 0.999, roughly nine percentage points inflation, consistent across seeds.
links.quote: These findings show that image-level splitting substantially overstates real-world performance, and that patient-wise, calibrated evaluation offers a more trustworthy basis for clinical deployment.

links.outcome: Performance across held-out hospitals in leave-one-hospital-out testing
links.effect: Performance held up reasonably well across held-out hospitals.
links.quote: performance held up reasonably well across held-out hospitals.

links.outcome: Sex disparity in sensitivity after pooling across patients
links.effect: No sex disparity in sensitivity found once pooled across patients, though one appeared spuriously at the image level.
links.quote: no sex disparity in sensitivity was found once results were pooled across patients, though one appeared spuriously at the image level.

links.outcome: accuracy and AUC under leakage-free versus leaky splits
links.effect: Patient-wise: AUC 0.946, accuracy 0.905; leaky image-level: AUC 0.999, accuracy 0.991; roughly nine percentage-point inflation.
links.quote: Under the patient-wise protocol, the detector achieved an AUC of 0.946, accuracy of 0.905, sensitivity of 0.889, specificity of 0.942, and Matthews correlation coefficient of 0.796, whereas the leaky image-level split raised accuracy to 0.991 and AUC to 0.999, an inflation of roughly nine percentage points that was consistent across seeds.

links.effect: Plain ResNet-18 performed comparably to hybrid model; convolution-free Transformer performed near chance.
links.quote: A plain ResNet-18 performed comparably to the hybrid model, while a convolution-free Transformer performed near chance, and performance held up reasonably well across held-out hospitals.

links.effect: Performance held up reasonably well across held-out hospitals; no numeric site-specific effect reported.
links.quote: A plain ResNet-18 performed comparably to the hybrid model, while a convolution-free Transformer performed near chance, and performance held up reasonably well across held-out hospitals.

links.quote: Calibration and selective classification further improved reliability, and no sex disparity in sensitivity was found once results were pooled across patients, though one appeared spuriously at the image level.

screen.practice: leakage-free patient-wise validation with calibration and uncertainty-based selective classification
screen.reason: Empirically investigates data leakage from image-level splitting vs patient-wise splitting, alongside calibration and conformal prediction as validation practices to avoid inflated diagnostic accuracy.

primary.practice: patient-wise data partitioning and calibration/uncertainty quantification
